message.content:
Based on my search, here is a comprehensive overview of the bones of the head (skull):

## Overview

The human skull consists of **22 bones** (or 29 if including the inner ear bones and hyoid bone). These bones are mostly connected by sutures (fibrous, immovable joints). The skull is divided into two main parts:

- **Neurocranium (cranial vault)** – protects the brain
- **Viscerocranium (facial skeleton)** – supports facial structures

---

## Cranial Bones (8 bones)

These form the protective housing around the brain:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Frontal bone** (1) | Forms the forehead and superior part of the eye sockets (orbits); contains frontal sinuses |
| **Parietal bones** (2) | Form the sides and roof of the cranial vault |
| **Temporal bones** (2) | Form the sides and base of the cranium; contain middle and inner ear structures; features include mastoid process, styloid process, and external acoustic meatus |
| **Occipital bone** (1) | Forms the back and base of the skull; contains the **foramen magnum** (where spinal cord connects to brain) |
| **Sphenoid bone** (1) | Butterfly-shaped bone at the base of the skull; contains the sella turcica (houses pituitary gland); articulates with almost all other cranial bones |
| **Ethmoid bone** (1) | Located between the orbits; forms part of the nasal cavity; contains the cribriform plate (allows olfactory nerves to pass) |

---

## Facial Bones (14 bones)

These form the structure of the face:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Mandible** (1) | Lower jaw; the **only movable bone** of the skull; houses lower teeth |
| **Maxillae** (2) | Upper jaw; form part of the orbit and most of the hard palate; contain maxillary sinuses |
| **Zygomatic bones** (2) | Cheekbones; form part of the lateral walls of the orbits |
| **Nasal bones** (2) | Form the bridge of the nose |
| **Lacrimal bones** (2) | Small bones in the medial walls of the orbits; house the lacrimal sac |
| **Palatine bones** (2) | Form the posterior part of the hard palate and part of the nasal cavity |
| **Inferior nasal conchae** (2) | Curved bones projecting into the nasal cavity; aid in airflow regulation |
| **Vomer** (1) | Forms the inferior portion of the nasal septum |

---

## Additional Associated Bones

- **Hyoid bone** – Located in the neck (not part of skull proper); supports tongue and larynx muscles
- **Auditory ossicles** (6 total: 3 in each ear) – malleus, incus, and stapes; located in the temporal bones

---

## Major Sutures (Joints Between Bones)

- **Coronal suture** – between frontal and parietal bones
- **Sagittal suture** – between the two parietal bones
- **Lambdoid suture** – between parietal and occipital bones
- **Squamous suture** – between parietal and temporal bones

---

## Key Functions

1. **Protection** – of the brain, meninges, cerebral vasculature, and sensory organs
2. **Support** – for facial structures and muscles of mastication and expression
3. **Passage ways** – numerous foramina allow cranial nerves and blood vessels to pass through

---

Sources:
1. https://www.kenhub.com/en/library/anatomy/the-skull
2. https://www.osmosis.org/learn/Bones_of_the_cranium
3. https://teachmeanatomy.info/head/osteology/skull/
4. https://www.numberanalytics.com/blog/skull-bones-anatomy-histology-explored
5. https://www.acibademhealthpoint.com/the-back-of-head-bones-understanding-cranial-anatomy/
6. https://anatomynote.com/the-human-skull-an-anatomical-masterpiece/
7. https://anatomy.co.uk/skull
